prompt: Use case: illustration-story. One original high-resolution master painting for a Sanskrit reader, part of a consistent 18-image Ishopanishad series. Square 1:1 canvas, request 2048 by 2048 pixels or the highest supported square resolution. Refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting. Use one coherent scene, no collage. Main narrative subjects MUST fit inside the central 60 percent of the width and central 50 percent of the height; surround them with generous low-detail sky, paper atmosphere and ground. Avoid important faces, hands and narrative objects near edges. This single master will be used behind live text in portrait and landscape on phones and tablets; surrounding atmosphere can crop, the scene must remain intelligible when fitted without cropping. Do not draw any Sanskrit, Roman text, verse numbers, typography, frame, border, watermark, infographic, UI, or page decoration. Do not portray a formless teaching as a specific deity unless the verse explicitly invokes that deity. Interpretive devotional illustration, not a literal historical reconstruction. Verse-specific source meaning from the app: The door of the True is covered with a golden disk. Open that, O Pushan, that we may see the nature of the True. Illustration: A radiant golden sun disk partially veiled by a thin luminous sheet of cloud, with a narrow opening revealing clear white-gold light beyond. A small contemplative observer below looks upward with reverence. Evoke the golden covering over the face of truth and the prayer to Pushan to uncover it; no giant human face or text in the sun.
